attributes.body_ja:
「もの」は、もともと「物（もの）」という意味（いみ）の名詞（めいし）です。これが文（ぶん）の終（お）わりで使（つか）われると、少（すこ）し強（つよ）い気持（きも）ちで理由（りゆう）を伝（つた）える終助詞（しゅうじょし）になります。この「もの」は「〜から」と同（おな）じように使（つか）います。とてもくだけた表現（ひょうげん）なので、フォーマルな場（ば）では使（つか）わないようにしましょう。

「もの」は、語（ご）の普通形（ふつうけい）の終（お）わりに使（つか）います。

「もの」をもっと強調（きょうちょう）したいとき、動詞（どうし）やイ形容詞（けいようし）のあとに「んだ」、ナ形容詞（けいようし）や名詞（めいし）のあとに「なんだ」を付（つ）けることがよくあります。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「もの」を「もん」と短（みじか）く言（い）う場合（ばあい）もありますが、この言（い）い方（かた）は、かわいらしく聞（き）こえたり、子（こ）どもみたいに聞（き）こえたりします。そのため、ふだんの会話（かいわ）ではあまり使（つか）わないほうがいいでしょう。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「んだもの」を少（すこ）し丁寧（ていねい）にすると、「んですもの」になります。この表現（ひょうげん）は、ふだんの会話（かいわ）ではあまり使（つか）われませんが、アニメや漫画（まんが）、小説（しょうせつ）などにはよく出（で）てきます。
attributes.body:
もの, an extremely common noun in Japanese that means 'thing', can also be used as a sentence ending particle. In these cases, it adds a small amount of emotion to a statement, and presents it as a reason. Due to this, もの is usually translated as 'because', or 'cause'. Literally, it just means 'it's an (A) thing!'. もの is quite casual, so should be avoided in formal situations.

To use もの as 'because', attach it to the end of the plain form of any word.

To emphasize もの even further, the explanatory んだ (after a verb or い-Adjective), or なんだ (after a な-Adjective or noun) will often be used.

Caution

もの can be shortened to もん in its use as a sentence ending particle. However, this makes the statement sound far more 'cute' or 'childish'. Due to this, it should be avoided in standard conversation.

Fun Fact

Although it is not used regularly in standard Japanese, んですもの is a slightly more polite version of んだもの that appears frequently in anime, manga, and novels.

attributes.body: Both もの・もん and ことだから can be used to give reasons, but they differ in tone and intent. もの・もん is casual, colloquial, and subjective, used to express personal feelings or justifications, like 'because (A)'. ことだから, on the other hand, has a more objective and emphatic feel, often meaning 'it is precisely because (A) that (B)'. In some contexts, ことだから can also imply 'considering (A), then (B)'.

These two are closely related and use the same もの (with もん as a more casual variant) to express reason. もの・もん is often used at the end of a sentence in a casual or even childish tone to give a personal reason, e.g. 'because (A)'. ものだから is a slightly more formal expression, often used to explain or justify an action or situation in a softer, less direct way.

These expressions also share the same root as もの・もん, but differ in tone and formality. もの・もん is casual and subjective, typically used for personal justifications like 'cause (A)'. ものですから or もので adds a more objective or polite tone, and is commonly used in formal or semi-formal situations when offering explanations or justifications for one's actions or circumstances.

attributes.body: なぜなら〜から and もの・もん are similar in that both can express a reason, but they differ significantly in tone and formality. なぜなら～から is a formal and objective way of stating a reason, similar to saying, 'as for why, it is because (A)'. In contrast, もの・もん is casual or colloquial, sometimes even childish, and conveys a personal, subjective tone, like saying, 'because' or ''cause (A)'.

attributes.body: ので expresses a cause or reason, similar to 'A, so B' in English. もの or もん (the latter being more casual) can also express a reason, adding emphasis or emotion, like the English 'because.' The main difference is that ので sounds more objective and can be used mid-sentence, while もの or もん typically comes at the end of a sentence and conveys a more personal or emotional tone.

attributes.body: から expresses a cause or reason, similar to 'A, so B' in English. もの or もん (with もん being more casual) can also express an emphatic or emotional reason, similar to 'because' in English. The main difference is that から can be used mid-sentence, while もの or もん typically appears at the end of a sentence and conveys a more personal or emotional tone.
